title: Wallpapering: preparation, lining, adhesives and roll formats
independence: No maker pays to appear here, and there are no affiliate links.

interpretation.housePractice: Our house standard where the wallpaper maker is silent.
interpretation.pasteScale: Strength steps are our house scale, not a rating shared by manufacturers.
interpretation.precedence: The wallpaper maker's instruction for the product always comes first.
interpretation.calculator: A quantity to order, not a set-out, and never a price.

houseRules.title: The maker's instruction comes first
houseRules.text: When the wallpaper maker names a primer, a lining grade or a paste for the product, we use what it names.

houseRules.title: Where the maker is silent, our house standard
houseRules.text: Walls are primed with Zinsser Gardz. Where lining is needed, it is Erfurt lining paper, hung with Wallrock Power Adhesive.

houseRules.title: We hang only with pastes we have tested
houseRules.text: We hang with the paste the wallpaper maker names, or one of the pastes listed here, which we have tested on our own jobs. Some other pastes we have tried let joints open and the top and bottom edges lift as the paper dried. It is easy to put right, but a client should never have to see it.

houseRules.title: Our house practice: the lining paste is at least one step above
houseRules.text: We use our own four-step scale to choose a lining paste at least one step above the wallpaper paste. This is Mr Wallcover's house practice, not a cross-brand manufacturer strength standard. When either paste is unknown or the wallpaper paste is at the top step, we check the combination before anything is ordered. The wallpaper maker's instruction takes precedence, including a requirement to use the same paste for both layers.

houseRules.title: Every lining roll is the same product and grade
houseRules.text: Lining paper has no batch to match, but every roll on a job must be the same product and grade, so the same thickness and the same shade of white.

makers.name: de Gournay

lining.printed: All walls should be lined with plain white 1000 or 1200 grade paper lining paper.

makers.liningPastePrinted: The lining paper should be hung with the same adhesive as will be used to hang the final panels (see 'paste' below).
makers.pastePrinted: Red Lidded Paste (type II) for non-woven papers that do not absorb much water; Yellow Lidded Paste (type I) for papers that require soaking.
makers.pasteName: de Gournay Red or Yellow Lidded Paste, as its instructions give for the paper
notes: Cross-lining is not needed so long as the joints of the lining do not meet the joints of the panels.
de Gournay will not accept claims for labour charges or other consequential losses under any circumstances.

makers.name: Cole & Son

lining.printed: A good quality, 800 or 1000 grade lining paper is recommended.

notes: Walls must be primed and if necessary cross line with lining paper.

We recommend lining walls where highly metallic papers are being installed. If lining paper is being installed it should always be hung horizontally, following manufacturer’s instructions, and be allowed to dry completely.
No claim for hanging costs in excess of one roll will be accepted.

makers.name: Farrow & Ball

lining.printed: we recommend that walls are horizontally cross lined with a good quality, midweight to heavyweight lining paper – around 1200–1400 grade – and left to dry for a minimum of 12 hours prior to hanging.

makers.pastePrinted: not recommended for non-woven (‘paste the wall’) wallpapers
makers.pasteName: Farrow & Ball wallpaper paste, only where the product’s hanging instruction permits it
makers.pasteCheck: Confirm the Farrow & Ball product and backing before choosing paste: its powder paste is not recommended for non-woven (‘paste the wall’) wallpapers.

pasteCoverage.printed: Each tube is suitable for hanging up to 5 rolls of Farrow & Ball wallpaper.

notes: Newly plastered walls and other absorbent surfaces should be carefully sized before hanging wallpaper.

makers.name: Fromental (printed non-woven)

lining.printed: For optimal results, apply 1000-grade lining paper, especially for lighter wallpapers, to prevent marks from showing through. Lining paper is not mandatory.

makers.pastePrinted: Use a premium-quality tub adhesive (pH-neutral, solvent-free, fungicide-protected, light-grade). Avoid self-mix adhesives, all-purpose, or heavy-duty pastes.
makers.pasteName: A premium light-grade tub adhesive, as Fromental asks
notes: Apply a PVA-based size to the walls, adjusting the thickness according to wall absorbency.

makers.name: Fromental (grasscloth)

lining.printed: We recommend cross-lining the walls with lining paper before installing grasscloth.

makers.pastePrinted: Use a good-quality pre-mixed wallcovering adhesive.
makers.pasteName: A good-quality pre-mixed wallcovering adhesive, as Fromental asks
notes: Do not over-soak the wallpaper. Keep adhesive and water off the face.

makers.name: Graham & Brown

lining.printed: Professional decorators hang lining paper horizontally. This is called cross lining.

notes: The paste must be the correct type for a traditional or a paste-the-wall paper.

makers.name: Muraspec
makers.liningPastePrinted: Murabond Heavy Adhesive must be used when hanging Lining Paper.
makers.pasteName: Murabond, in the grade Muraspec’s leaflet gives for the design
notes: Never use material from different batches on one wall.
Cut and hang in roll sequence; do not in-fill with off cuts or out of sequence drops.
Remove all existing wallcovering and backing papers. (Hanging leaflet, May 2026)
On coated non-absorbent walls: "rub down the wall to provide a key. Hang the wallcovering using Murabond Sealed Surface Adhesive." (Hanging leaflet, May 2026)

makers.name: Phillip Jeffries
notes: Apply material above doors and windows as it comes off the roll; do not skip.
…the material should be inspected after three (3) strips are installed.
No claims will be allowed for more than (3) strips on the wall.

makers.name: Vescom
makers.pasteName: Vescom adhesive: 1000, 2000, 2500 or 3000, by the wallcovering's weight and the wall
notes: Completely remove existing wallcoverings and backing papers.
Keep adhesive and water off the face.

makers.name: Tektura
makers.pastePrinted: Generally Tekfix Plus, though depends on substrate.
makers.pasteName: Tekfix Plus, as Tektura asks (Tekfix VOV round right-angled corners)
notes: Tektura publishes no data sheet for its Tekfix pastes, so a lining under Tektura is checked with us first.

wallTypes.name: New skim plaster
wallTypes.treatment: Let it dry through, and confirm with a moisture reading, not the calendar. Cole & Son asks for two or three weeks.
wallTypes.primerNote: Gardz's data sheet: allow new plaster to cure at least 24 hours before applying it.
wallTypes.inspect: Always take a moisture reading before covering.

wallTypes.name: Old lime plaster
wallTypes.treatment: Historic, breathable fabric. Treated case by case with the wallpaper maker's instruction and, often, the specifier.
wallTypes.inspect: Always. No standard treatment is given here.

wallTypes.name: Taped-and-jointed plasterboard
wallTypes.primerNote: Gardz's data sheet: it seals drywall facing paper and joint compound, and protects the board when the wallcovering is stripped later.
wallTypes.inspect: Only if the facing paper is torn or the joints show.

wallTypes.name: Painted: matt emulsion
wallTypes.treatment: Clean. Scrape and sand anything loose.
wallTypes.primerNote: Gardz's data sheet: it binds chalky, builder's flat paint to the wall.
wallTypes.inspect: If the paint lifts on a scratch test.

wallTypes.name: Painted: vinyl silk or oil-based
wallTypes.treatment: Walls painted with gloss or a vinyl silk emulsion are checked on site before a treatment is chosen.
wallTypes.inspect: Always: the treatment depends on what the paint is and how well it holds.

wallTypes.name: Stripped, previously papered
wallTypes.treatment: Old backing and paste residue removed.
wallTypes.primerNote: Gardz's data sheet: it seals in residual wallpaper paste.
wallTypes.inspect: If the plaster under the old paper is loose or cracked.

wallTypes.name: Cement render and blockwork
wallTypes.treatment: Alkaline, and often too rough to paper directly: skimmed or heavily lined first.

wallTypes.name: MDF, timber and ply
wallTypes.treatment: Joints and movement decide the build-up; paper on joinery is a specification of its own.

wallTypes.name: Existing lining paper
wallTypes.treatment: Kept only if it is sound and firmly stuck at every edge; otherwise stripped and relined. de Gournay says not to prime on top of its lining.
wallTypes.inspect: Always: a lining that is letting go takes the new paper with it.

conditions.name: Sound, clean and dry
conditions.lining: Only where the wallpaper maker asks for it.

conditions.name: Chalky or flaking
conditions.treatment: Scrape and sand off anything flaking, then bind the surface. Gardz's data sheet: it binds down chalky surfaces.
conditions.lining: As the wall needs, once it is sound.

conditions.name: Sealed or non-porous: gloss paint, an existing vinyl
conditions.treatment: Washed, degreased and keyed as the wallpaper maker permits. We confirm a compatible sealed-surface or vinyl-over-vinyl adhesive (VOV) for the product and wall. Muraspec and Vescom require old wallcoverings and backing papers to be removed. Any fire classification applies to the specified complete build-up; check the product's current instructions.
conditions.lining: Only with an adhesive the lining maker accepts on a sealed surface.

conditions.name: Damp: rising, penetrating or condensation
conditions.treatment: The cause is found and fixed first. Nothing is papered over damp.
conditions.lining: Not until the wall is dry.

conditions.name: Stains: water, smoke or nicotine
conditions.treatment: The cause of a water stain is fixed first. Stains are then sealed with a stain-blocking primer, then primed.

conditions.name: New alkaline surfaces
conditions.treatment: New plaster: left to dry, then Gardz (rated to pH 12.5 on its data sheet). Cement render and blockwork: an alkali-resisting primer.

conditions.name: Cracks and filler
conditions.treatment: Cracks raked out and filled, filler sanded flush, then primed. A heavier lining bridges fine cracks; it does not hold a moving one.
conditions.lining: Erfurt MAV 1200 for minor cracks, 1400 for larger cracks, 1700 or heavier for damaged plaster.

conditions.name: Uneven porosity
conditions.treatment: Primed so the paste dries at one rate everywhere. A lining paper gives one even, absorbent surface.

conditions.name: Out of true
conditions.treatment: Lining does not straighten a wall. It is made good first, or the set-out allows for it.

conditions.name: Mould
conditions.treatment: Mould means a moisture problem. The cause is dealt with first.
conditions.lining: Not until the cause is fixed.

conditionQuestion.label: What are the walls like now?

vov.title: Vinyl-over-vinyl adhesive (VOV)
vov.text: Vinyl-over-vinyl (VOV) and sealed-surface adhesives have product-specific uses. Some are intended for hanging on non-porous surfaces; others are for overlaps, borders or repairs. We select one only for the uses its maker allows, with the wallpaper maker's instruction first. They sit outside our house paste scale.
